title: The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary -- Ch. 14: Update on Death Penalty Cases
link: The Bio-Age Dawns on the Judiciary (book)
primary_topics: Chapter 14 'Update on Death Penalty Cases': CJP's continuing survey of death-penalty jurisprudence and implementation during his eighth year on the Court
sub_topics: No executions during his eighth year (reprieves granted by President Arroyo)
People v. Echegaray upheld the Death Penalty Law (RA 7659) six years earlier
Survey of the year's capital cases (Delim, Rullepa, Abrazaldo, and others)
CJP's continuing reservations about the death penalty
signature_phrases: No Executions During My Eighth Year in the Court

stances.claim: Though the Court upheld the Death Penalty Law in Echegaray, implementation stalled (no executions during the year owing to reprieves), and CJP continues to voice his reservations.

notable_anecdotes: No actual executions were carried out during his eighth year; scheduled executions were postponed by presidential reprieves.
one_paragraph_summary: Chapter 14, 'Update on Death Penalty Cases,' continues CJP's yearly survey of capital-punishment jurisprudence. He reports that no executions were carried out during his eighth year (owing to reprieves granted by President Arroyo), recalls that People v. Echegaray upheld the Death Penalty Law (RA 7659), surveys the year's capital cases (Delim, Rullepa, Abrazaldo, and others), and reiterates his continuing reservations about the penalty.
